I find the discussion here to be slightly myopic. It is obvious he did something wrong, it is also obvious that members of the government and other actors likely knew about all of this for several years. You aren't the CEO of a trillion dollar company without being under the eye of many people. The real question people should be asking is "why now?" why is the PR spectacle happening at this moment and who is benefitting from supplying the NYTimes with this compromising information.

Obviously we can only come up with conjecture, but it should at least be discussed that this is not happening out of thin air due solely to his reckless actions but represents some kind of hidden power struggle. It's quite clear to me folks like Secretary of State Marco Rubio very likely knew about these things taking place for quite some time.

The story was broken by the New York Times. New York Times journalists Tripp Mickle and Ana Swanson got a tip from from "a tech industry contact"[1] in August. They worked sources and investigated until they were ready to break the story in October.

Based on the photos that have been popping up, the tech industry contact could have been any one of the comparatively large number of people in position to observe what was going on.

atdt 2026/11/13 11:34
Of course it was not as simple as that. Investigative reporters earn their keep. They spoke to a lot of sources, including sources in US intelligence. But that is not unusual for any important story: people in government like to talk, even those who work in three-letter agencies, for a mix of personal and professional reasons.

Your comment above implies that the answer to "Why now?" is: "Because covert powers so decided." There is nothing in the story that disproves that, but also nothing that requires it. The initial tip could have been ordered from above, but it could just as easily have come from any one of dozens if not hundreds of people, motivated by just about anything: grievance, envy, high-mindedness, malice, vanity.

Jensen's conspicuously close relationship and public sightings with Alice Huang were already on the radar of an observant Hindenburg Research-esque short seller firm back in May:

NVIDIA (NVDA): The China Problem

https://culperresearch.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Culper...

It uses careful language to avoid implying/defaming anything that couldn't be supported by publicly verifiable info but clearly found their relationship questionable to say the least.

It certainly didn't need a strategic CIA leak or House of Cards style knife in the back to doom Jensen. Embarrassing in retrospect how poorly they concealed it.
